title: Append-only, with tombstones and lineage
subtitle: Durable logs are only ever appended, deletion is a mark, and every derived artefact can prove where it came from
lede: When the history of what happened can be rewritten, recovery becomes archaeology. I build the durable state in my systems as append-only logs. Completion or deletion is a tombstone written in place, in a fixed order relative to the data it refers to, so that a crash between two writes is repaired by a scan rather than a guess. Every derived artefact, an index, an extraction, a projection, carries a hash or a reference back to its source, so lineage is a property of the data and not a convention. Writes append. A segment or a table is never rewritten in place except for the tombstone mark.
quote: I pay both, because the alternative is a second bookkeeping file that can disagree with the data.
evidence: Append-only log design: memory-mapped append-only segments where completion is a tombstone written at the entry's offset and recovery reads only tombstones.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: a fixed write order, output persisted before the tombstone and the input retired last, so every recovery path is a scan.
Data provenance and lineage: derived indexes, extractions and projections carry the identity of their inputs, checked at build, persist and load and refused on mismatch.
author: Corey James
